title: frp tunneling
desc: Expose internal services to a public server with frpc, or run frps locally as the server
tokenClientPlaceholder: Must match the token of frps
userPlaceholder: Optional; used as a proxy name prefix
proxiesDesc: The frpc instance restarts automatically after changes
bindAddrHelp: Address the frpc connection port listens on. Set 127.0.0.1 when frps sits behind a reverse proxy such as Gately and frpc connects over websocket / wss
tokenServerPlaceholder: Strongly recommended; frpc must use the same token
proxyBindAddrHelp: Address the HTTP / HTTPS ports and the remote ports of tcp / udp proxies listen on
allAddrs: Leave empty to listen on all addresses
allowPortsPlaceholder: e.g. 6000-6100,7500; leave empty for no limit
firewallHelp: Ports frps listens on must be opened in your firewall and router; map them when deploying with Docker.
importTip: Supports legacy frpc.ini / frps.ini (with a [common] section) and toml from frp 0.52+. Importing into an existing instance keeps its enabled state; a new instance is created disabled, so enable it manually after checking.
pasteHint: Or paste the config content below
pastePlaceholder: Paste the content of frpc.ini / frpc.toml
modeAppend: Append (proxies with the same name stay unchanged)
subdomainPlaceholder: Requires a subdomain host configured in frps
secretHelp: The visitor side must use the same key
noClients: No frpc instances yet. Add one to connect to an frps server
confirmDeleteClientProxies: Delete this frpc instance and its {count} proxies?
pastePlaceholderServer: Paste the content of frps.ini / frps.toml
